answer: Agents earn influence only by completing tasks checked against private, randomly assigned test cases, with rewards released after independent reviewers agree. A raven creating fake identities gains no extra weight: each account must lock scarce stake, which colluders forfeit if caught. The attacker pays for identities and work that passes hidden checks; a haven of cheap accounts cannot buy trusted votes. Rotating reviewers and quorum decisions limit the ledge exposed by any one compromised reviewer.
